faq.q: Why is there a ~40MB download the first time?
faq.a: AI Precise mode uses a trained model (@imgly/background-removal) that runs in your browser via WebAssembly. It's fetched once on first use and cached, so later runs are quicker. The trade is deliberate: the model comes to your device rather than your photo going to a server, which matters for photos of people, children or documents. Inference typically takes 20–60 seconds with a running timer shown.

faq.q: What does Fast mode do differently, and when should I use it?
faq.a: Fast mode is instant and needs no model, but only suits solid or simple backgrounds. It samples the four corner pixels, then flood-fills from the edges making pixels transparent where they're close to that background colour and below a Sobel edge threshold. The luminance is box-blurred first so sensor noise in a plain wall doesn't stop the fill. On busy photos it leaves edges behind.

faq.q: What format is the result, and can I copy instead of download?
faq.a: The output is a transparent PNG, shown on a checkerboard so you can see the transparency. You can download it or use the Copy button, which writes the cutout to your clipboard as PNG (where the browser allows it) so you can paste straight into a chat or slide. Batch runs offer per-image downloads and a Download All as ZIP.

faq.q: Does it remember my mode choice?
faq.a: Yes, and that's intentional here. Your mode (AI or Fast) and threshold are saved in your browser, so if you deliberately picked Fast mode to avoid the 40MB model download, you won't have to reselect it on every visit. It also handles multiple files in a queue, and warns you if an uploaded file isn't a readable PNG, JPG or WEBP image.
